body.p: In the Office Action, claims 1-8 and 10 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor regards as the invention. Specifically, the claims were alleged to be indefinite because several terms either lacked antecedent basis or were not clearly defined.
As indicated above, Applicant has amended the claims to correct issue relating to lack of clarity and lack of antecedent basis.
In view of the foregoing, withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) rejections is respectfully requested.

Additionally, claims 1-4, 6-8 and 10 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by McClain (US 2,293,656). Claim 5 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over McClain, and further in view of Uprety (US 2017/0150659).

Claims 1-2, 4, and 7-8 were also rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Tondu (PCT/FR2020/052123, while US 2022/0410539 is referenced for convenience). Additionally, claim 5 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Tondu, and further in view of Uprety. Finally, claims 6 and 10 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Tondu, and further in view of McCarthy et al (US 2015/0047275). Applicant respectfully traverses the foregoing rejections and requests reconsideration.

With respect to claim 1, the Office refers to pg. 1, col. 2, in. 24-27, pg. 2, col. 1, in. 45-50, pg. 4, col. 1, in. 20-22, and FIGs. VIII-XI of McClain as disclosing all of the features of claim 1 of the present application. Office Action page 3. While Applicant does not agree, McClain discloses an aircraft windshield having two glass sheets or other hard transparent material and an intermediate layer of a plastic material between the glass sheets. McClain pg. 2, col. 1, ln. 20-27, see Fig. VIII.

The Office alleges that McClain anticipates claim 3 and discloses an outer ply is attached to the coating layer via a glue, where the glue is "glass bonded to the plastic." Office Action page 3. Applicant does not agree because McClain does not disclose glue or adhesive, but instead discloses a bonding between two layers. This does not disclose the use of a separate glue. See Verdegaal Bros. v. Union Oil Co. of California, 814 F.2d 628, 631, 2 USPQ2d 1051, 1053 (Fed. Cir. 1987) ("A claim is anticipated only if each and every element as set forth in the claim is found, either expressly or inherently described, in a single prior art reference") (emphasis added). Therefore, McClain does not disclose of a glue that attaches the coating layer to an outer ply.
The Office refers to [0045] and Figure 1 of Tondu as disclosing all of the features of claim 1 of the present application. Office Action pages 4-5. Applicant does not agree.

Tondu discloses aircraft windshield laminate having two plastic sheets and an intermediate adhesive layer, where the adhesive layer enwraps a sheet of glass. Tondu [0049], see Figure 1. The Office alleges that Tondu anticipates claim 1 because Tondu discloses that the plastic sheet, PMMA, covers the entire surface of the ply including the peripheral edge, "extends beyond peripheral edge," citing to Fig. 1. Office Action pages 4-5; Tondu [0049], see Figure 1. However, as shown below, Fig. 1 of Tondu does not show that either PMMA layer 1, 3 covers the entire surface of the glass 4, including the peripheral edges. Specifically, as seen in Fig. 1, the PMMA layers 1, 3 do not cover the peripheral edges (in the boxes) of the glass 4.

Further, Tondu does disclose of an adhesive layer, however, Tondu does not disclose that the glass sheet is entirely coated with a coating layer of viscoelastic transparent organic material, including a peripheral edge thereof, or that the adhesive layer attaches the coating layer to an outer ply.

Accordingly, since claim 1 includes features that are neither disclosed nor suggested by the cited art, claim 1 should be allowable over same. Those claims that depend therefrom or refer thereto should be allowable as well - at least by virtue of their claim dependency.

Applicant therefore respectfully submits that all of the claims of the application are allowable and thus requests that the Examiner indicate all of the claims as allowed and pass the application to allowance.

The amendments to the claims and cancellation of claims was done merely to expedite prosecution of the present case. Applicant reserves any and all rights to pursue the subject matter of the original claims in this application, or in another application. Moreover, these amendments should not be construed as an admission or acquiescence to any rejection.

Furthermore, the fact that Applicant has only addressed certain rejections should not be considered to be acquiescence to the rejections. Rather, Applicant has presented the argument herein in an effort to expedite prosecution. Applicant reserves any and all rights to address any rejection made but not specifically addressed herein.
